commits.message:
feat(misc#340): serialize deploy workflows with concurrency groups (#584)

Part of the ephemeral PR environments epic
(CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#321), the backend half of
CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#340; the ui half is CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui#729,
merged 2026-09-11.

Every deploying workflow (orchestration dev, impl, prod, and both manual
deploys) now declares a concurrency group with cancel-in-progress false,
so runs queue instead of racing for shared Terraform state and never
interrupt an apply mid-flight. Dev, impl, and the manual deploys key on
the ref, so pushes to the same PR or branch serialize and a superseded
pending run is dropped. Prod keys on the literal group
orchestration-prod plus the merged flag, so an unmerged close lands in a
different bucket and cannot evict a pending prod deploy. The
infrastructure job additionally carries a deploy-<env> group with queue
max so applies from different PRs, or from a manual deploy and a PR,
queue FIFO on the same environment and a third PR no longer cancels the
second.

The ECR lifecycle change that was in this PR is gone. A lifecycle
preview showed the keep-last-4 rule counting protected pr-* images and
expiring every bare-SHA deployable instead, and ECR selection cannot
exclude a prefix, so PR images move to their own dev repos in #586 and
ztmf/api's policy is unchanged.

Known edge: two dev PRs can still interleave their backend jobs so one
apply reads the other's SSM tag. Cosmetic in dev and retired when
misc#345 makes dev main-only.

Verified: all workflows parse. No application code or Terraform changed.
commits.author: cameron testerman

commits.message:
feat(misc#341): per-PR environment Terraform root and the /pr/* edge behavior (#586)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#341. Part of the ephemeral PR
environments epic (CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#321). Consumes the test
image from #583 and the frontend image from CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui#730;
driven by the workflows in ztmf-misc#342 and #343.

New leaf root infrastructure/pr-env, one instance per PR with state
keyed pr/<repo>/<n> in the dev state bucket. It reads dev's cluster,
ALB, listener, VPC, and Okta client by name and creates only per-PR
resources: a Fargate task with the API in test mode, a Postgres sidecar
from ECR Public, and the nginx frontend serving under /pr/<repo>/<n>/; a
one-task service with steady-state wait so a crash loop fails the apply;
an HTTPS target group; one ALB listener rule at 10000+n (ztmf) or
20000+n (ui) that authenticates with the dev Okta client and forwards
only the PR prefix; a 7-day log group; two random secrets in SSM; and
roles scoped to those parameters plus ECS Exec. Everything is tagged
with the repo and PR number.

Main root: a pr_env_enabled flag, true in dev only, adds the /pr/*
CloudFront behavior on the internal-ALB origin in the same
forward-everything, TTL 0 shape as /api/*, and creates the ztmf/ui ECR
repo with the same pr-* lifecycle rule as ztmf/api. The ECR repo goes
beyond the ticket's "behavior only" wording because the pr-env root's
data source needs it to exist and nothing earlier creates it.

Verified: fmt, validate, and tflint clean on both roots. Read-only plan
against dev shows the ui repo and policy created, the distribution
gaining the /pr/* behavior, and the web-assets bucket policy rewritten
to identical content (its document embeds the distribution ARN). Live
apply and destroy of ztmf/9999 and ui/9999 environments will be recorded
in a comment once the main-root change has applied to dev.

Update 2026-09-14: PR API images move to a new dev-only repo,
ztmf/api-pr, instead of sharing ztmf/api. A lifecycle preview run for
#584 showed the keep-last-4 rule counting protected pr-* images and
expiring every bare-SHA deployable instead. ztmf/api-pr holds
pr-ztmf-<n>-<sha> and the main-<sha> test-target build a ui PR runs;
ztmf/ui holds ui-<sha> and pr-ui-<n>-<sha>. Both use a prefixed
keep-last-4 above a 14-day age rule, previewed on a scratch repo with
the expected result. ztmf/api's policy is unchanged. api_image_tag now
requires one of the two prefixed shapes.

commits.message:
chore(rollover): remove the FY2026 hard-code, carry its dedup forward (ztmf#502) (#590)

Closes #502. **Draft until the FY2026Q4 cycle closes**, per @danielbowne
on the issue — the override is already inert, so holding the merge only
preserves the delete-and-recreate recovery path.

## Summary

The FY2026 rollover hard-code from #501 is no longer needed: FY2026
exists, there is one unified cycle again, and `findPreviousDataCall` is
correct on its own. This removes it, keeps the one load-bearing line it
contained, and fixes the accounting that line breaks.

- **Removes** the hard-code block, its call site, the `pgxpool` import,
and `TestMatchesRolloverHardcodeTarget`
- **Keeps** its `DISTINCT ON` — the only dedup guard in the rollover
path — by lifting it into the permanent copy
- **Adjusts** the anomaly accounting, which would otherwise false-alarm
on every duplicate collapse

## What this removes

In `backend/internal/model/`:

- `scores.go` — the `TEMPORARY HARD-CODE - ztmf#500` block
- `scores.go` — the call site at the top of `copyPreviousScores`
- `scores.go` — the `pgxpool` import, used only by
`earlierRolloverHardcodeTargets`
- `scores_test.go` — `TestMatchesRolloverHardcodeTarget`

The last two are not optional; leaving either fails the build. No schema
change, no migration, nothing to unwind.

## The dedup guard

`scores` has no uniqueness constraint on `(fismasystemid, datacallid,
functionid)`, so a source cycle holding two answers to one question
copies both.

- Carried forward because **this** is the PR that deletes it — deferring
to #491 opens a regression window for as long as that takes
- Not theoretical: both FY2026 sources carry duplicates (81 and 120
questions) and FY2026 came out with zero
- Winner is `(s.status = 'done') DESC, s.scoreid DESC`. `status` must
outrank `scoreid`, which is creation order, not edit order — otherwise
an untouched carried twin can beat the row the ISSO actually answered
- A discard, not a merge: 47–70 duplicates per cycle hold genuinely
different answers, and the loser does not travel forward

## Why the accounting changed

`copied` was compared against a plain `COUNT(*)`, one number covering
both a real under-copy and FK-dropped rows (ztmf#411). Dedup underneath
that reads as partial on every healthy rollover, firing a wired
CloudWatch alarm exactly when the guard works.

- Three counts now: `candidates` (all source rows), `resolvable` (FK
parents intact), `expected` (what the dedup copy should emit)
- Fires on `copied < expected || resolvable < candidates`, so each
failure keeps its own signal
- The one-line alternative — `expected` as a `COUNT(DISTINCT)` — joins
away unresolvable rows and silently removes an alarm that exists today
- `ROLLOVER_ANOMALY` token unchanged, so no infrastructure change

### Reading a ROLLOVER_ANOMALY

`resolvable < candidates` fires on source rows whose `functionoptionid`
no longer resolves. This is **not new** — `main` alarms on the same rows
today, because the old `copied < expected` caught them as a short copy —
but the fields now say which case it is:

- `copied == expected` with `unresolvable > 0` → the copy was complete;
a known dead-FK drop is the trigger, no action beyond cleaning the
source rows
- `copied < expected` → a genuine under-copy, whatever `unresolvable`
says

Such rows do exist despite all three FKs reporting `convalidated = t`,
since bulk loads run under `session_replication_role = replica` and
bypass FK triggers. Measured on the dev stack: **FY2025 Q3 holds 33,
every other cycle holds zero — including FY2026 ZTM**, which is what the
next rollover reads. So this is not expected to trip on the next cycle.
Worth confirming against prod before merge:

```sql
SELECT COUNT(*) FROM scores s
LEFT JOIN functionoptions fo ON fo.functionoptionid = s.functionoptionid
WHERE s.datacallid = <previous cycle> AND fo.functionoptionid IS NULL;
```

## Acceptance criteria (#502)

- [x] FY2026 data call exists in prod; rollover validated; ISSOs
answering
- [x] `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `gofmt -l` clean
- [x] `make test-unit` green
- [x] `make test-integration` green, including against #583's baked-seed
image after rebase
- [x] `grep -rn "rolloverHardcode\|ROLLOVER_HARDCODE\|OpDivHardcoded"`
returns nothing, checked repo-wide
- [x] Still rolls forward by deadline, still emits `ROLLOVER_ANOMALY` on
a zero or partial copy
- [x] The open `DISTINCT ON` decision made explicitly rather than by
omission

## Relationship to #491

- Satisfies its **"rollover cannot introduce or propagate duplicates"**
criterion — flagged so it is not built twice
- Does **not** close it: the write path still branches on `ScoreID == 0`
with no natural-key lookup, there is still no uniqueness constraint, and
existing duplicates are untouched
- The winner rule is **provisional and belongs to #491** — changing it
is one line

## Testing

Three integration tests over a shared fixture, each verified by mutating
the production code rather than by passing once:

- **Dedup is per question** — keyed on `fismasystemid` alone the copy
collapses a system's whole answer set to one row and reports success;
that mutation passed the entire suite before a second question was added
to the fixture
- **The answered row wins** — without the status term it carries `"stale
carried twin"` forward
- **A collapse is not an anomaly** — against the old arithmetic it fails
with `expected=1 copied=1 candidates=2`. A sentinel line proves the log
capture is live so the assertion cannot pass vacuously

Only the alarm's silence is asserted; neither firing condition is
reachable from a test. Generated SQL inspected directly: one bind
parameter, no user input in either interpolated fragment.

**Reviewers:** CI's Backend job is gated on `draft == false`, so only
Analysis has run. First full run happens when this leaves draft.

## Not fixed here

- Inserts now land in `(fismasystemid, functionid)` order, so new
`scoreid`s are assigned in a different sequence. Only the answers export
reads `scoreid` ordering, as a tiebreak within one (system, function)
pair — unaffected
- Existing duplicates in closed cycles keep double-weighting pillar
scores; the scoring aggregate's `answers` CTE is not de-duplicated. That
fan-out is #491's

commits.message:
fix(#587): reject duplicate system acronyms within an OpDiv (#589)

Closes #587.

The API now rejects a system acronym that another live system in the
same OpDiv already holds, on both create and update. The comparison is
case-insensitive and whitespace-trimmed, and decommissioned systems are
ignored so a retired acronym can be reused. A rejected save returns 400
with the offending acronym under `data.fismaacronym`, the same shape
every other field validation uses.

Why this matters: the acronym is the human key for a system everywhere
it is shown and linked, including the questionnaire URL. Seven IHS
systems arrived from the FY26 inventory load with the placeholder
acronym "Pending", so every questionnaire link for any of them resolved
to the lowest-id one. ISSOs saw another system's completed answers and
believed their own were saved. Nothing was lost, but the collision cost
a day of triage and a data call extension.

Why the check lives in `Save` rather than a unique index: prod currently
holds four active same-OpDiv duplicate groups (two systems each entered
twice, one pair of genuinely different systems sharing an acronym). A
partial unique index would fail to apply on prod and on dev until those
are resolved, and a failing migration crash-loops the deploy. The
application check works immediately and blocks any new duplicate
regardless of how the data looks. The index follows in a separate
migration once the four groups are cleaned up; that cleanup is a data
decision for the OpDiv admins, not something a migration should make.

The OpDiv used for the comparison is resolved the way `Save` writes it:
the stored row's OpDiv on update (the column is not updatable, so an
`opdiv_id` in a PUT body must not redirect the check), the explicit
`opdiv_id` on insert, and the CMS default when neither applies. The
acronym is also stored trimmed now, so padding cannot survive into the
display key.

Reactivation gets the same guard. A decommissioned system's acronym is
free for reuse, so bringing that system back while a live one holds the
acronym would recreate the collision; the reactivate endpoint refuses
with the same 400 until one of them is renamed. Every other write path
either goes through `Save` or never touches the acronym or the
decommissioned flag.

The one thing a reviewer should weigh: the check and the write are not
in one transaction, so two simultaneous creates could both pass. On an
admin-only surface that is acceptable as a best-effort guard; the unique
index is the real serialization and follows once the existing duplicates
are cleaned up.

## Riders

Two partial-PUT bugs surfaced while adjusting the suite and are fixed
here as separate commits. Both are the same shape: a column written on
every update, so a PUT that omitted the key clobbered it.

- `sdl_sync_enabled` was a plain bool, so an omitted key wrote false and
silently dropped the system out of the data lake sync. It is now a
`*bool`: false on insert when omitted, written on update only when the
request carried the key (the controller already tracks key presence for
the tri-state booleans).
- `fismaacronym` was written unconditionally, so an omitted key cleared
it to an empty string. It is now written only when the request carries a
non-blank value.

No behavior change for requests that send the fields.

## Testing

- Emberfall: a second POST reusing an acronym with different casing and
padding returns 400; a PUT that renames a system onto an acronym another
live system holds returns 400; a PUT that keeps the system's own acronym
still succeeds (no self-collision); reactivating a decommissioned system
whose acronym a live system now holds returns 400, and succeeds once
that system is retired.
- The HHS test system in the suite gets its own acronym (`ZTMF-HHS`)
rather than relying on case order to avoid colliding with the first test
system.
- Emberfall for the riders: a PUT that omits `sdl_sync_enabled` leaves
it as stored; a PUT that omits `fismaacronym` leaves it as stored.
- `make test-unit` and `make test-e2e` pass on every commit (230 cases
at the tip).
- No OpenAPI change: the 400 response shape is the existing validation
error, and no annotations changed. `make generate-openapi` produces no
diff.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Partial unique index on `(opdiv_id, lower(btrim(fismaacronym))) WHERE
NOT decommissioned`, after the four existing duplicate groups are
resolved.
- ztmf-ui#732 routes the questionnaire by system id so acronym edits
stop breaking links at all.

commits.message:
fix(misc#384): scope the data-call export to the catalog the dashboard scores (#588)

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#384.

## What

HRSA reported BHP-TAP exporting 50 rows for a 25-question questionnaire
while the dashboard and questionnaire both correctly reported 25. Both
copies of every question were answered, so the workbook offered two
answers per question with no way to tell which one the score came from.

The export was not reading the wrong data call — `FindAnswers` pins the
call id in three places and `datacallid` is a PK, so both sets are FY26.
What differs is the question catalog. BHP-TAP's `datacenterenvironment`
changed mid-cycle, and because `scores` stores an answer as a
`functionoptionid` rather than as (question, tier), the answers already
recorded became unreachable from the new environment's `functions` set;
the team re-answered all 25. The export's functions join was
applicable-OR-answered (#528), so it admitted both catalogs and emitted
a row for each.

Reproduced on dev, which still has BHP-TAP on AWS with its answers on
the AWS catalog: switching the system to SaaS orphaned all of them and
the export returned 25 rows, one per SaaS question, no orphaned rows.
That also confirms the trigger rather than inferring it from the
exported text.

No other surface widened. Scoring's `expected` CTE derives functions
from the system's current mapped environment, and `/scores/progress`
restricts `questionsanswered` the same way (`dce.scoring_key =
f.datacenterenvironment`), which is why dev's BHP-TAP reports 0 of 25
answered there too — the export now agrees with it.

The functions join resolves each system's applicable functions the same
way scoring does. The answered branch survives only as a fallback for a
system with no applicable catalog at all — an unmapped environment, or
one retired to the DECOMMISSIONED marker whose `scoring_key` is NULL.
Dropping it outright would export nothing for those systems instead of
their recorded history, which the decommissioned-or-answered guard
already pins.

`scores.scoreid` is added to the `ORDER BY`. A duplicate score row on a
single function (ztmf#491) ties on every other sort key and the two
copies can carry different notes, so the export could present a
different answer first from run to run. Systems without duplicates emit
rows in byte-identical order to before, since the tie never arises.

Measured on the dev stack (993 systems, 134,911 scores) against FY2026
ZTM: a SaaS system holding orphaned answers goes 50 rows to 25, an AWS
one 80 to 40, and systems without orphaned answers stay at 40, zero
duplicated questions either way. The whole-call export also got faster,
2.28s to 1.43s, since the added `NOT EXISTS` prunes more candidate rows
than it costs — worth noting given the 47s regression migration 0055
fixed. No score moves; the scoring query is untouched and the dropped
rows were never in its `expected` set.

Two consequences worth knowing before support fields a question.
Immediately after an environment change and before anyone re-answers,
the export is a blank questionnaire — that is what dev showed, it
matches the 0-of-25 the questionnaire already reported, and the answers
remain in `scores`. And a decommissioned system whose answers are all on
a retired catalog now exports no rows at all rather than its old
answers.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **Rows from more than one data call, with query and counts** — No,
impossible by construction as above. FY26 is 50 rows / 25 questions x2,
both answered; FY25 ZTM is 40 rows, all blank.
2. **Which `datacallid` each set belongs to; is the export scoping** —
Both FY26. Scope is applied in the `datacalls` join, the `scores` left
join, and the answered branch, all from the URL path and set after query
decoding so `?DataCallID=` cannot override it (misc#268). Same
`questionid`, different `functionid` and `functionoptions`.
3. **Blast radius** — BHP-TAP is the only HRSA system with this
signature; the other 42 of 45 export one row per question and none
exports a blank block. NMDP and IntegrityM also over-export at 80 rows,
but from duplicate rows on the *same* option — ztmf#491, not this. A
228-system export from another OpDiv showed no instance. The same pivot
on remaining OpDivs is outstanding.
4. **Which year scoring reads; is FY26 authoritative** — FY26. The
dashboard's 3.47 and all four pillar scores match the
current-catalog-only computation exactly (orphans alone 3.76, all 50
blended 3.62), `questionsexpected = 25` rules out a duplicated catalog,
and BHP-TAP's 25 (Pillar, Function) keys match HRSA's 13 other SaaS
systems. The dev reproduction above independently confirms the
environment change as the trigger.
5. **Relationship to ztmf#491 and misc#336** — Separate causes. 23 of 25
pairs sit on different option text and 13 share tier and score across
the two catalogs, only possible with two catalogs; no pair has
byte-identical notes. #491 is the inverse: same option, same tier and
score, notes usually byte-identical.
6. **Written answer for HRSA posted to the issue** — drafted, not yet
posted; the comment for ztmf-misc#384 still needs to go up.
7. **Fix scoped or linked ticket opened** — this PR.

## Verification

The `#528` orphaned-answer assertion pinned the behavior this ticket
reverses, so it now asserts those answers do *not* export, counting
expected answered rows in SQL and skipping systems under a
reduced-pillar rule. The decommissioned-or-answered guard resolves its
expected count the way the export now admits rows, counting score rows
rather than distinct functions so a #491 duplicate is not miscounted,
and a new case covers the combination both blocks could otherwise miss:
decommissioned, still mapped, and holding orphaned answers.

`TestFindAnswersScoringParityIntegration` is new. It derives each
system's expected row count from scoring's applicable set, allowing more
than one row where a duplicate score row exists, and compares against
the export over a bounded sample that puts orphan-holding systems first.

`answerOrderKeys` in the ordering test now includes notes. Its previous
key of acronym/pillar/function compared equal however two duplicate rows
came back, so it could not detect the instability `scoreid` was added to
prevent.

Gate: `make test-unit` green, `make test-integration` green, `make
generate-openapi` no drift. No API shape change, so no frontend work
needed.

## Not fixed here

NMDP and IntegrityM stay at 80 rows. Their duplicates are two score rows
on one `functionid`, arriving through the scores left join, and unlike
orphaned rows they *do* reach the dashboard — the scoring aggregate's
`answers` CTE is not de-duplicated, so both copies land in the pillar
`AVG`. A `DISTINCT ON` in the export would hide that rather than fix it,
so it is left to #491 where I have flagged the fan-out.

Orphaned answers are excluded from the export but retained, per the call
on this: not wanted in the workbook, but not deleted. Retention is
unaffected — this is a read-only change to one join predicate, the rows
stay in `scores`, and `FindScores` reads that table with no catalog
filter so `GET /scores` still returns them. That also settles the
alternative floated on the ticket: marking orphaned versus active rows
in the workbook is not needed, so #384's export-columns option is out of
scope.

There is no audit trail for an environment change — `fismasystems` keeps
no history and system edits are not written to `events` — so while dev
reproduces the mechanism, the specific edit on prod cannot be recovered
after the fact. Filed separately.

Assert the SYSTEM_DELEGATE recipient set, not just a 201 (#585)

The SYSTEM_DELEGATE mass-email case asserts only that the POST returns
201, and `SaveMassEmail` returns 201 with an empty recipient list when a
group resolves to nobody. That empty-audience path is deliberate — it
exists for groups where every user is contactless — but it means the

matches no rows, no mail is sent, and the case still passes.

READONLY_ADMIN already got recipient-content coverage in #580.
SYSTEM_DELEGATE, the group that actually outgrew `VARCHAR(5)`, had only

empire seed is reached, and the OWNER and read-only admin tiers are not.

commits.message:
Convert srcutils fetchers to query hooks (#736)

* refactor(vocab): cache the system-attribute vocabulary for the session

useSystemAttributes refetched on every mount, and both consumers are
modals. It is now a useQuery under a new vocabularyQueryOptions export
on queryClient, shared with the two vocabularies migrating next.

staleTime alone is not enough: unobserved queries are collected after
five minutes, so a modal would refetch on reopen. gcTime: Infinity is
what keeps a remount off the network.

Failure still resolves to a silent empty list, as before. The hook
returns a shared constant rather than a fresh [] per render. Consumers
are untouched. createTestQueryClient moves to test-utils.

Gate: typecheck, lint:js, test:ci (1068 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failures).

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* refactor(opdivs): serve OpDivs and environments from session-cached queries

Title fetched both lists through hand-rolled effects. They now come from
useOpDivs and useDataCenterEnvironments under vocabularyQueryOptions. The
context shape is unchanged, so no consumer moved.

useCreateOpDiv and useUpdateOpDiv invalidate the shared list on success
without awaiting the refetch, so the dialog still closes on the write.
OpDivAdmin drops its refreshOpdivs calls; the delegate toggle waits for
the delegates commit.

The Title suites stub axios by URL rather than the fetcher, since a hook
calls its module-local binding and a mocked export never reaches it.
EMPTY_LIST replaces three per-file constants; queryWrapper and
renderWithQueryClient join test-utils.

Gate: typecheck, lint:js, lint:other, test:ci (1075 passed, 3 skipped,
0 failures).

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* refactor(users): read and write OpDiv grants through query hooks

`useUserOpDivs` refetches on mount because grant assignments determine the permissions an administrator can assign. `useSetUserOpDivs` updates the cache directly from the successful response payload; because the `PUT` endpoint overwrites the entire grant set and rejects invalid assignments, an immediate refetch is unnecessary.

`OpDivGrantModal` isolates user edits in local state to prevent background refetches from overwriting active changes. The `OpDivs` column in `UserTable` uses per-row queries enabled only when inline grant data is absent, replacing both the override map and `Promise.all` backfill logic. Cached query entries persist across unmounts so grant sets remain available during grid scrolling.

`QueryHookOptions` replaces `VocabularyQueryHookOptions`, adding `staleTime` and `gcTime` settings. This uses a plain type definition because spreading a `Pick` of generic query options widened response types to `{}`.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* refactor(delegates): read and write system delegates through query hooks

Migrates two queries and four mutations in `delegates.ts`. `addSystemDelegate` and its `skipAuthHandling` comment remain untouched. The candidate search query retains previous search results while a new search term loads.

Every write operation invalidates the delegate roster and all cached candidate lists using a shared key factory. Roster invalidation is awaited before closing dialogs to ensure the UI renders the updated list, matching previous behavior, while candidate cache invalidations run in the background.

`SystemDelegatesSection` removes its local roster state and both fetch effects. The `OpDivAdmin` toggle becomes a mutation, eliminating the last caller of `refreshOpdivs` and allowing its removal from the Outlet context. Component test suites stub Axios directly rather than mock fetchers, confirming end-to-end interceptor bypass for the capability-off 403 response.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* fix(users): read OpDiv grants inline and invalidate on save

The grant-save mutation seeded the user's cache entry with the request
body. A scoped admin's body carries only the OpDivs they hold and the
backend preserves the target's other grants, so the seed was a subset
of the stored set and the users table dropped chips the user still had.
It now invalidates the entry; the modal refetches on its next open.

The per-row fallback fetch in the OpDivs column served a list row
without assignedopdivids, which the backend never emits. The cell, its
staleTime/gcTime overrides, and the gcTime and staleTime members of
QueryHookOptions are gone. The column reads the row, and the post-save
row refresh patches grants from the user detail alongside
identity_provider, which is the authoritative set for every caller.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* fix(users): stop a reconnect from restarting the grant read

The grant modal treats any in-flight read as its initial load: it blanks
the picker and disables Save. A reconnect refetch mid-edit therefore
stranded the admin's changes, and one that failed left Save disabled for
the rest of the open with the edits still on screen, so the only exit was
Cancel.

The read now opts out of refetch-on-reconnect. Open and a change of user
stay the only fetch triggers, which is what the modal already assumed.
The other queries on this branch are unaffected: the vocabularies never
go stale, and the roster and candidate search both render fine through a
background refetch.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* test: make the query-hook suites prove what their comments claim

Three cases asserted less than they said.

The two vocabulary remount tests unmounted and remounted in the same
tick, which no collection window can elapse across, so they passed on
the client default and proved only staleTime. They now advance fake
timers well past five minutes between the two mounts; dropping gcTime to
the default fails them.

The delegate roster test asserted the refetch through waitFor, which is
satisfied whether or not the write waited for it. It now serves a
different roster on the refetch and checks the cache at the instant
mutateAsync resolves, so voiding the returned invalidation fails it.

The OpDivAdmin suite stubbed three fetchers that the hooks never call,
since each hook binds its module-local import. The stubs are gone, and
the save path they were meant to cover is now exercised for real through
the axios adapter: a create that POSTs the trimmed form, and a 400 whose
field map lands on the Code field instead of a toast.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* fix(delegates): scope the picker to its system and to one search per attach

Three narrow corrections to the section and the grant dialog.

The detail page stays mounted when the route moves between two systems
already in the shared list, so the delegates section kept the previous
system's search term and candidate rows, and an attach from that list
posted to the new system. The section is now keyed by system id.

Attaching ran two candidate searches: the write invalidated every
candidate list, refreshing the typed term, and clearing the input then
switched keys and refreshed again, discarding the first result. The
search is cleared before the write instead, and restored if the attach
fails so a guard message still leaves the person on screen to retry.

The grant dialog dropped staged edits on open and close but not on a
change of target. The current caller closes before switching users, so
nothing was reachable, but the guard costs a dependency and stops a
future caller from writing one user's selections onto another.

The first has no test: asserting a key means driving the whole detail
page through two systems, which is out of proportion to a one-line
guard. The other two are covered.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* fix(delegates): read the roster fresh on every mount

Caching the roster under the generic stale time was a regression: the
section refetched on every mount before this branch. The roster is the
shared user-to-system table filtered to delegates, and the pages that
change it are elsewhere. A role edit or a system assignment moves someone
on or off it, and both still write through raw requests that invalidate
nothing, so a cached roster could list a delegate the server no longer
has.

The generic stale time suits reference data. This is operational data
another page edits, the same reasoning that already gives the OpDiv grant
read a zero stale time.

The candidate search keeps the default. Every term the user has not just
typed is a new key and so a new request, each write here invalidates the
lot, and a stale entry is self-correcting because the backend rejects an
attach for someone no longer eligible. Zeroing it would also refetch on
each return to a previous term, including the cleared one after an
attach, undoing the single-search fix.

Proper invalidation from those write sites belongs with their own
migration.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* fix(users): resolve grant save and row refresh edge cases

A failed post-save row refresh only logged, leaving stale grants and a
stale identity provider on screen with nothing to say so. It warns again
and stays non-blocking. The comment above it also claimed a second call on
modal close that does not exist, which would have suggested a failure can
warn twice.

The grant save's invalidation refetched into a modal that closes on the
next line, a second GET per save whose result was discarded. refetchType
none marks the entry stale instead; the zero stale time still refetches
on the next open.

The one-toast-per-open guard reset on open alone, so a dialog pointed at a
new target in place would swallow that target's failed read. It now resets
on a change of targetId too, matching the staged-edit reset beside it.

Also drops the deleted older-backend fallback from the userOpdivs module
doc and a redundant assertion in the delegates suite.

Gate: typecheck, lint:js, lint:other, test:ci (83 suites, 1093 passed,
3 skipped, 0 failures).

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* test(users): drop the merged backfill tests the grant migration removed

#723 landed on main alongside this branch and pinned the per-user grant backfill and the userOpDivMap override, both deleted here. The override test is covered by the detail-repaint test; the backfill test now pins the replacement: a row without assignedopdivids shows the placeholder and fires no per-user read.

Refs CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#357

* fix(delegates): scope retained candidate rows to their own system

Review follow-ups on #736.

useDelegateCandidates held rows across any key change, systemId
included. The detail page keys the section by system, but that made one
line the only thing between a reader and another system's candidates,
and attaching one posts to the system in the path. Rows are now held
across a change of search term only. Tests at the hook and the section;
both fail if the scoping is reverted.

refreshUserRow skips its stale-row warning on an auth-handled error,
matching every other catch on the branch. useUserOpDivs names `enabled`
and keeps policy last, like its siblings. useSystemAttributes drops a
parameter no caller passed; the key factory still models the dimension.
The grant modal's comment now covers the failed re-read it was silent
about.

Gate: typecheck, lint:js, lint:other, test:ci (1102 passed, 3 skipped,
0 failures).

* docs(data-fetching): move hook rationale out of the docblocks

Review follow-up on #736: the branch leaned on long comments to carry

fix(ui#714): clear the frostfall 508 findings and enforce the gate (#737)

* fix(ui#714): clear the frostfall 508 findings and enforce the gate

All 24 open code scanning alerts are fixed at their source, so the
baseline prunes to empty and the ci profile enforces serious-or-worse
from here on.

The 15 aria-required-children alerts were two distinct defects. MUI X v6
puts role="grid" on the DataGrid root, which also holds the toolbar and
the pagination footer - a grid may only own rows and rowgroups, so the
search box, switches, and page-size combobox all counted as children
that are not allowed. useAccessibleGrid moves the grid semantics onto
.MuiDataGrid-main, which wraps exactly the headers and the row groups;
that is the relocation MUI made upstream in v8. The other twelve were
the users grid's actions cells: the buttons already carry role="menuitem",
but the <span> wrapping the disabled Delete button (needed for Tooltip to
see hover on a disabled control) did not, so the cell's role="menu" had a
child that was not a menu item.

The color-contrast alerts were the header's "Scoring Tool" at 3.06:1 and
the dashboard's outlined warning chips at 3.1:1. The comparison Select in
the pillar scores modal now takes its name from the "Compare with:" label.

Closes CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-ui#714

* fix(ui#714): adopt MUI's ariaV7 and keep the SARIF on failing scans

Review follow-ups.

make frostfall-ci ran the enforcing pass before the SARIF pass under
bash -euo pipefail, so the first new violation aborted the recipe before
frostfall.sarif existed and the if: always() upload failed on a missing
file - losing the report that says what broke, on exactly the runs that
need it. The SARIF pass now runs first, and with --profile none: the ci
profile would otherwise apply expect to a pass that reads an empty
baseline by design, failing the job for a violation the baseline
deliberately grandfathers. Verified by reintroducing the contrast
violation: old order exits 1 with no SARIF, new order exits 1 with a
4-result SARIF.

experimentalFeatures={{ ariaV7: true }} is MUI's own version of what the
hook was doing by hand, and the default from v7 on. It puts the aria
attributes on .MuiDataGrid-main natively and corrects cells from
role="cell" to role="gridcell". That retires the MutationObserver, the
role demotion, and the forwardedProps mutation hazard with it. What the
flag does not do is carry the grid's name: aria-label still lands on the
root, which ariaV7 leaves generic, so the hook now does only that.

EventsTable adopts the hook too. Its route cannot join the scan config -
the seeded user has no unscoped read, so the page renders nothing and the
test would error rather than pass.

The self-delete guard dims its button and drops the ripple, so a refused
click reads as refused now that it is not natively disabled.

* test(ui#714): put the events grid under the 508 gate

The earlier claim that this route could not be scanned was wrong: it was
scanned at /#/events, which is not a route. It lives at /#/admin/events,
and the gate in front of it is unscoped read, which the seeded Test.User
holds as OWNER. Nothing about the seed was in the way.

The test has teeth: with the hook removed from EventsTable the page
reports the same critical aria-required-children the other grids did, and
with it the six-test run is clean.

* fix(ui#714): gate the questionnaire and fix its chip contrast

The questionnaire is the app's one long editable form and the surface a
scorer spends the most time on, so it goes under the gate: seeded system
DS-1, anchored on the <h1>, which is the question text itself and so only
exists once the payload has rendered. Its default state scans clean, as do
questions 2-4 reached by clicking through.

Two chips on that route fail AA in states the seed cannot reach, so the
scan cannot see them: the carry-forward "not yet confirmed" chip (outlined
warning, 3.11:1) and the AI Summary badge (outlined info, 3.86:1). Both are
the defect already fixed on the dashboard, so the darkened values move to
src/utils/chipStyles.ts and the dashboard chip now reads from there too.
The test computes the ratios rather than restating the hex values, so a
later nudge back under 4.5:1 fails there instead of in a scan.

Outlined success and error already clear AA and stay with the palette.
SystemEnrichmentCard's filled warning chip is the same class of defect on
the system-detail route and is NOT fixed here - filled chips fail on their
background rather than their label, which is a different change.

feat(misc#343): nginx image for PR environments (#730)

* feat(misc#343): nginx image for PR environments

Builds the bundle with VITE_IDP_ENABLED=false into nginx 1.27 behind a
self-signed cert on 443. Serves the path-agnostic bundle under PR_PATH_PREFIX,
proxies the prefixed api/ path to API_UPSTREAM, and mints the config.js bearer
token for TEST_USER_EMAIL from AUTH_HS256_SECRET at container start. Nothing in
dev or prod consumes this image.

Part of CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#343 and the epic CMS-Enterprise/ztmf-misc#321.

* feat(misc#343): keep cookies out of the PR environment proxy

PR environments share dev's host, so a dev ztmf_session cookie reached
the PR API, was checked before the bearer, and 401ed every call; and
logout's host-scoped Set-Cookie clears reached the browser and dropped
the user's dev and ALB sessions. The image is bearer-only, so the proxy
now strips Cookie inbound and hides Set-Cookie outbound.

Also: 301 the slashless prefix the ALB rule routes to the trailing-slash
form with relative redirects so the port survives, serve /healthz with
one Content-Type, fail the entrypoint when PR_PATH_PREFIX is unset, and
note in the README that IdP-enabled paths are not exercised.

* test(UserTable): assert the column-definition wiring, not just that it runs

The grid mock already invoked each column's valueGetter and renderCell, but
nothing asserted on the output, so the wiring was uncovered: a swap from the
code map to the label map, a dropped unknown-id fallback, an inverted IdP
placeholder, or the raw ISO string threaded into the last-seen cell would all

Verified by mutation: each of those four changes to UserTable.tsx now fails at

* test(UserTable): pin the grant precedence and the non-rendering column props

Review found two gaps the first pass left open, both inside the scope this
change set out to close.

The opdivs cell reads userOpDivMap before the row's inline assignedopdivids,
and that order is load-bearing: refreshUserRow updates the map after a grant
edit but never patches the row, so the inline value goes stale and the map has
to win. Every earlier test populated only one of the two sources, so reversing
the precedence passed the whole suite. The new case puts a legacy row next to
a normal one, which backfills every row and makes the two disagree for the
same user.

renderEditCell, the identity_provider select options, and the last-seen sort
comparator are invisible to a rendering assertion, because the grid mock only
calls valueGetter and renderCell. Dropping any of the three left the suite
green. The mock now exposes the column definitions it was handed so those
properties can be asserted directly.

Verified by mutation: reversing the precedence, dropping renderEditCell,
changing the IdP column off singleSelect, and dropping the comparator each
fail a test now, and each passed before.

Introduce tanstack query for datafetching (#727)

* feat(query): configure TanStack Query and application providers

Install TanStack Query and its development tools, then add a shared
QueryClient configured with a one-minute stale time, one retry, and no
window-focus refetching.

Wrap the application with QueryClientProvider and expose the closed-by-
default devtools only in development builds. Extend the shared test
renderer with a fresh no-retry client per render so cached server state
cannot leak between tests, and cover the application query defaults.

* refactor(api): centralize endpoint paths and query keys

Add canonical API path factories for every Axios endpoint so dynamic routes, query variants, and leading-slash conventions live in one place. Replace raw endpoint strings across views, utilities, auth flows, downloads, and mutations without altering their transport, cancellation, error handling, or `skipAuthHandling` behavior.

Add hierarchical TanStack Query keys that preserve response-shaping parameters and provide stable list and detail prefixes for cache invalidation. Centralize repeated score, export, and system-resource URL construction, and update affected tests to assert against the shared path factories.

* fix(query): retry only transient failures, never a 4xx

The blanket retry: 1 retried definitive server answers, and 401 was the
sharp case: the Axios interceptor reacts to it by navigating to the
login flow, so the retry fired a second doomed request into the
interceptor while that redirect was already underway. It also meant the
enrichment endpoint's expected 403/404 answers would each fire twice.

The default is now a function: one retry for network errors, non-Axios
errors and 5xx responses, where the next attempt can genuinely succeed;
no retries for any response below 500, which is the server saying
something rather than failing to answer.

* docs(api): record the URL-joining and encoding constraints in keys

Two facts a future reader needs before touching this module. The
leading-slash paths are safe only because Axios joins baseURL and path
by string concatenation; fetch or new URL semantics would resolve them
against the origin and silently drop /api/v1. And withQuery encodes
spaces as + where Axios params would write %20, which agrees today only
because no current parameter carries a space.

* build: fail production builds that bundle the query devtools

The devtools-absent-from-production contract cannot be a Jest test:
import.meta.env.DEV and NODE_ENV substitution happen at build time, so
a unit test only ever sees the development branch. This check runs
after vite build --mode production and greps the emitted bundles for
markers only the devtools carry.

Verified in both directions. The current build passes. Deleting the
main.tsx DEV gate alone does NOT trip it, because the package's main
entry already exports a no-op outside development; what does trip it,
exit 1, is importing the deliberate always-on
@tanstack/react-query-devtools/production entry, which is the realistic
way devtools would ever reach production.

* docs(keys): clarify URL encoding behavior in query parameters

* refactor(system-detail): fetch enrichment data with TanStack Query

Replace SystemEnrichmentCard's hand-written request effect and local loading, error, and response state with useQuery. Key enrichment reads by FISMA UID, forward Query's cancellation signal to Axios, and flatten the pipeline response envelope before exposing it to the existing card rendering.

Preserve the request-local auth bypass and existing UI behavior: 403 and 404 remain quiet empty states, unexpected failures retain the failed-load message, and the ISSO update PUT remains imperative. Extend the component tests to verify skipAuthHandling and cancellation when the query unmounts.

* feat(query): standardize error handling and document data fetching

Add a shared QueryCache error callback that suppresses interceptor-handled auth errors, cancellations, unobserved requests, and queries with inline error states. Normalize other query failures through `parseApiError` and `notify` once, with duplicate prevention keyed by the query hash.

Expose a `QueryClient` factory so production and component tests share the same cache behavior while tests can disable retries. Add integration coverage for a 401 raised inside a query function, including redirect behavior, retry suppression, and protection against duplicate toasts. Pin `skipAuthHandling` at all five sanctioned call sites.

Document query-key conventions, cancellation, invalidation, query and mutation usage, Axios interoperability, and session-bootstrap exceptions. Fix formatting in the production devtools assertion script.

* fix(query): address review findings on data-fetching migration

TanStack Query retains the last successful `data` payload when a background refetch fails, populating `error` at the same time. `SystemEnrichmentCard` evaluated `error` in isolation, replacing populated Insights panels with red error text during failed refreshes. While `refetchOnWindowFocus` is disabled, `refetchOnReconnect` remains active, making network interruptions reaching two 5xx responses sufficient to trigger this state. Main avoided this behavior by omitting background refetches entirely and relying on an effect keyed on `fismaUid`. The guard now checks `error && !notFound && !enrichment`, and `docs/data-fetching.md` documents this retained-data behavior to ensure consistent implementation across remaining views.

This commit addresses additional items identified during review:

* **`apiPaths.scores.list` path enforcement:** Restores rejection on missing identifiers. Because `withQuery` drops `undefined` values, omitting a system ID stripped the filter parameter and returned scores for all systems in the data call. Callers folded these results into a function/option ID-keyed map, yielding invalid data instead of throwing a explicit error. `export` and `questions` narrow parameter types to prevent `undefined` values from reaching URL builders.
* **`FismaTable` export URL parameter handling:** Prevents `FismaTable` from substituting active data call IDs into export URLs. `exportCallId` evaluates to `null` when selections span multiple data calls; substituting values via `??` generated downloads containing mismatched data call responses. While disabled button states cover primary interaction paths, the click handler now exits early on `null` values.
* **`keys.ts` docblock correction:** Corrects `keys.ts` documentation stating `baseURL` is `/api/v1/`. The relative value `api/v1/` allows single build artifacts to serve behind PR environment prefixes. Integration test mock configurations are updated to match.
* **Cache key identifier normalization:** Normalizes identifiers in cache keys using `keyId` string conversion so `detail(42)` and `detail('42')` resolve to identical cache entries. This prevents invalidation mismatches caused by mixed string route parameters and numeric call sites.
* **Devtools dependency isolation:** Moves devtools to `devDependencies` and transitions loading to dynamic imports. Static imports added devtools to runtime dependency graphs evaluated by Snyk and SBOM scanners. Vite converts the `import.meta.env.DEV` ternary to `null` during production builds, omitting devtools chunks from output.
* **Devtools build assertion coverage:** Adds devtools build assertions to `build:dev`. Previous execution was restricted to `build:prod` within production orchestration pipelines, allowing regressions to pass merge validation. Assertion failure messaging now specifies the always-on `/production` entry point and packaging requirements.
* **Test suite corrections:** Fixes two questionnaire test suites matching `url.startsWith('scores')` against leading-slash paths, which previously passed by returning empty default payloads. Corrects `delegates.test.ts` mock parameters where test descriptions asserted capability-off rejections while mock setup returned 201 responses.

Refs #619
